title.narrative: ACTED: Building resilience in Syria 2025-2027 - ACTED 2025-2027 - ISK

description.narrative: Livelihood and resilience building in Syria.

The objectives of the project can be divided as follows:
Outcome 1: Local actors are supported to shape decision-making processes and participation:
Output 1.1: Participatory area-based research and community planning is implemented in all areas of intervention
Output 1.2: Local partners are supported to participate and shape key services and recovery efforts
Output 1.3: Area-Based Approach is strengthened across Syria
Under this outcome a number of Area-Based-Approach (ABA) assessments and updates will be made, technical support activities, gender profiles produced as well as conflict analysis reports. Joint coordination platforms will be established for interested partners to strengthen the ABA coordination. Local NGOs and local partners in the different ABAs will receive training. Technical support activities will be provided to NES Forum's area-based-coordination mechanisms and meetings will be organised with UN, INGOs and donors for a transparent dialogue, lessons-learned and coordination for resilience building in Syria.
Outcome 2: Opportunities for economic recovery of the areas are strengthened:
Output 2.1 Improved livelihoods through the promotion of income-generating activities and skills development
Output 2.2 Enhanced capacity of farmers through sustainable practices and improved community-based agricultural services and infrastructure
Under this outcome households will be supported with short term income generating opportunities, MSMs, incl. agri-business and will be supported through grants and training. Women and youth will be offered vocational training and start-up grants to support business or job placement. Farmers will receive training in climate-techniques and financial inputs based on Farmer Field Schools model to boost local production and enhance food security. Farmer associations will get capacity building and technical departments receive both training and some tools/equipment. Communal assets will be rehabilitated.
Outcome 3: Access to basic services for conflict-affected population is increased:
Output 3.1: Enhanced access to and management of sustainable, safe water and sanitation services
Output 3.2: Expanded groundwater monitoring capacity to inform the development of a water resource management plan
Output 3.3: Rehabilitated social infrastructure (i.e. key public facilities) aligned with the CRRP's findings
Under this outcome small, medium and large-scale water supply and waste-water assets and systems will be rehabilitated. WASH facilities in public schools upgrades and technical departments providing public basic services will get training and tools/equipment. Other examples; roads, electricity grids rehab, market sites, road lights, public parks, sport halls etc.
